answer: An agent market can resist Sybil attacks with earned capacity: new agents start throttled to tiny orders and gain higher limits only through work attested by counterparties. A comet must be tracked before its orbit is trusted, and so must an identity: history builds slowly and cannot be forged overnight. The nectar of the market, high-value contracts, flows only to agents with a long attestation trail. An attacker must pay the full cost of real work for each fake identity, so faking many costs more than it earns. A zephyr of new identities arrives daily, but none can move serious volume yet.
